messages:
ashley: ran a couple of nsys traces on the low-latency bench, saw one kernel eating ~58% of GPU time, surprised by the name. attaching the short summary below.

ashley: nsys summary (filtered by pid):
```
Total GPU time: 64.2 ms
mm_attn_softmax_forward: 37.5 ms (58.4%)
kv_pack_kernel: 8.1 ms (12.6%)
layernorm_fwd: 6.9 ms (10.7%)
kv_prefetch: 4.2 ms (6.5%)
other tiny kernels: 7.5 ms (11.8%)
```

ashley: occupancy samples show mm_attn has low SM occupancy (22%) but high warp stalls on memory. nvprof flame looked like lots of L2 misses.

sam: thanks — which model and sequence length? is this from the batching stress bench or production trace?

ashley: bench, llama-7b variant, seq=1024, batch=8 steady state. also saw that mm_attn spikes when KV cache hits drop (cache miss ratio ~18%).

raj: curious: mm_attn_softmax_forward is our fused softmax+dropout kernel, right? Historically it's compute heavy but usually memory-bound for long seq. could be a quantization path issue.

mike: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet (PNG) or the perfetto slice IDs? quick look at kernel launch params would help. also include cudaGetLastError logs if any.

ashley: pasted timeline to #eng-runtime-assets (link) but here is the kernel launch sample I copied from the trace:
```
mm_attn_softmax_forward<<<grid=(256,1,1),block=(256,1,1),shared=2048>>>(Q, K, out)
input bytes: 1.2GB/s, achieved bw: 220GB/s, L2 load: high, s_mem_read throughput: low
```

ashley: note shared mem usage jumped when batch grew to 8 -> causes register pressure and serialization on older SMs.

zoe: is this on pre-emptible nodes or dedicated? pre-emptible VMs caused some weird scheduling in the past.

ashley: Dedicated, p4d-equivalent machines. single process pinned to GPU.

raj: two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection picked the fallback non-optimized softmax (vectorized path) for seq=1024, 2) KV cache miss pattern forces per-token recompute/loads. want to triage by reproducing with smaller seq and toggling cache.

sam: try running nsys with environment VARS: RUNTIME_KERNEL_DEBUG=1, NN_BYPASS_VEC=1 to force the other kernel and compare. also collect nvtx ranges around KV lookup.

ashley: will do. scheduled a short run now (nsys sample + nvprof) and will post results.

(infra-bot): job 2141-annot-3 started on runner-19 (nsys collect)

ashley: quick follow-up after rerun — when forcing the vectorized kernel we see lower L2 miss rate but much higher register spilling and overall latency goes up ~1.3x. baseline vectorizable path wasn't chosen because of occupancy tradeoff.

mike: that points to kernel selection heuristics picking for lower registers -> more memory ops. maybe our selector weightings favor kernel A by latency at small seq but here batch/big seq flips the trade.

raj: propose we add a microbench sweep that enumerates (seq_len, batch, kv_hit_rate) combos and captures kernel runtime + L2/SM metrics. then feed into selector cost model.

zoe: also worth adding a cheap sampling in the runtime: if KV hit drops below threshold mid-rollout, switch to the high-occupancy kernel variant for the active request tranche. fallback must be fast (<2 token windows).

ashley: agreed. I'll add an experiment: dynamic kernel switch after detecting >10% KV misses over last 100 tokens. will measure latency outliers and tail p99.

sam: one more ask — can you attach the exact nsys command and the trace export name so I can reproduce?

ashley: nsys profile --output=ash-ns-2141 --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx=true --force-overwrite --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas && nsys export --report=summary ash-ns-2141.qdrep

ashley: last note: observed a perf regression vs last week's build: mm_attn_softmax_forward used to be ~28% of GPU time, now 58%. suspect a regression in kernel selection or a new compile flag that changed vectorization. filing a follow-up PR to add instrumentation. :memo:

mike: ack. if you want help diffs, ping me. also tag eng-runtime and eng-runtime/bench in the PR.

ashley: thanks — will post the sweep results tomorrow.
